findings.issue: The doc says the persisted `blocked_stop` row carries `gateResults` as named sub-records keyed by `convergenceGate`, `dimensionCoverageGate`, `p0ResolutionGate` and the rest, each with a `pass` boolean plus gate-specific fields (score, covered/missing, activeP0, ...), and that `the reducer reads these verbatim and does not coerce shapes`. The producer emits a row array instead: `step_emit_blocked_stop` binds `gate_results_array_json` as `One {gateId,status,reasonCode,evidenceDigest} row per legal-stop gate` and writes that same value to both `gateResults` and `gateDetail`; the ledger projection copies `gateDetail` into `gateResults`. So a reader who follows this bullet to `gateResults.dimensionCoverageGate.missing` (the custom-dimension coverage list the bullet advertises) finds an array of rows with no `pass` field, and the reducer's dashboard section does `Object.entries(entry.gateResults)` and reads `result.pass`, printing `?` for every gate. The JSON example above the bullet shows the same keyed shape and also carries `mode`, `sessionId` and `generation` fields that the projection does not write.

evidence.out:
1359:          - gate_results_array_json: "One {gateId,status,reasonCode,evidenceDigest} row per legal-stop gate (convergenceGate, dimensionCoverageGate, p0ResolutionGate, evidenceDensityGate, hotspotSaturationGate, claimAdjudicationGate, fixCompletenessReplayGate, candidateCoverageGate, graphlessFallbackGate), with at least one fail row when decision == BLOCKED"
225:          gateResults: (data.gateDetail ?? data.gateResults ?? {}) as JsonValue,
2693:            ? Object.entries(entry.gateResults)

findings.issue: The section 4 STATE FILES table presents itself as the packet's file list and omits the frontier node store, even though the same cheat sheet documents `--depth-mode=expansive` in sections 1 and 8. `state-format.md` counts `frontier-nodes.jsonl` as the tenth packet file for an expansive run, `frontier-admit.cjs` names it as its node store and is its only writer, and `reduce-state.cjs` reads it from the review directory to project `registry.frontier`, so an operator triaging an expansive run has no row pointing at the file that holds node status.

fix.new:
| Pause | `review/.deep-review-pause` | Sentinel | Pause between iterations |
| Frontier nodes | `review/frontier-nodes.jsonl` | JSON Lines | Node store for `--depth-mode=expansive`; a default run never creates it |

findings.issue: The finding-registry field reference gives `dimension` a closed list of the four canonical names. The reducer derives each finding's `dimension` with `deriveDimension(..., universe)`, where `universe` comes from `buildDimensionUniverse(config)` and appends every configured custom name after the canonical four, so a finding made on a configured custom dimension is recorded with e.g. `dimension: "performance"`, which this row says cannot happen.

fix.old: | dimension | string | Primary dimension: correctness, security, traceability, maintainability |
fix.new: | dimension | string | Primary dimension: correctness, security, traceability, maintainability, or any configured custom dimension name |
